note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count and address below comes from one City of St. George page, its Pickleball page, where a four-line list headed "City of St. George Pickleball Courts" gives each venue a name, a street address and a court count. The same page carries the City's 2025 programme schedule for Little Valley, a check-in rule, and an article dated 19 August 2020 that is used here for history and nothing else. Where the City is silent - on lighting, surface, hours and parking at every venue, and on price at two of the three - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: St. George publishes nothing about parking at any of these three venues. The word does not appear in the City's four-line court list, which gives each venue a name, a street address and a count and nothing more, and it does not appear in the 2020 article or the programme schedule on the same page. This site does not fill that gap from a map or an aerial photograph, and it does not fill it from the scale of the place either, though the scale is worth stating: Little Valley Pickleball Complex has thirty-three courts, and on the City's schedule two tournaments a year take "All 33 Courts" from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. over three or four days. Where a hundred and thirty-two players can be on court at once, the City's silence about where they leave their cars is a real gap, and it is recorded as one. Nothing is said about restrooms at any venue either. St. George's page is a programme page rather than a park amenities page, so the lists of shelters, restrooms and walking loops that other cities publish do not exist here. What the City does state about arriving is a rule rather than a lot. At Little Valley, "Players, please check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available during the St. George Pickleball programs". So the first thing to find on arrival is not a parking space but the attendant.
slots.peak_hours: The City publishes no opening hours for any of its pickleball courts and no closing time, and for Vernon Worthen Park and Bloomington Park it publishes nothing about timing at all. For Little Valley it publishes something more useful than opening hours: a full programme schedule, headed "St. George Pickleball Program Schedule / 2025", which says which courts are reserved, when, and for what. Winter League runs from 6 January to early March on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday mornings from 9:30 to 11:30 a.m. and evenings from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m., with Wednesday evenings running to 9:30, and each of those sessions reserves "9-32 (24 courts)". Youth sessions on Monday and Wednesday afternoons, 4:00 to 7:00 p.m., take "21-22, 26-29 (6 courts)". Adult clinics take two courts, 27 and 28. Spring League repeats the pattern from 24 March into May, with mornings from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. Two tournaments take everything: the Rock N Roll Tournament, 6 to 8 February, and the Southern Shootout, 2 to 5 April, each "All 33 Courts" from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. On a league morning or evening the schedule reserves courts 9 to 32 and leaves the other nine unreserved; during a tournament nothing is. The City adds that "Times may change based on participation numbers" and asks players to "check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available". It states nothing about lighting anywhere, so although it schedules play until 9:30 p.m. in January, this site records lighting at Little Valley as not stated rather than inferring it from a timetable. The schedule is dated 2025 and the page was read in September 2026, so treat the dates as the shape of the year rather than this year's calendar.
slots.surface_condition: The City names no surface anywhere on its pickleball page. The court list gives a name, an address and a count per venue, and the only descriptive words about the courts themselves are in the 2020 article, which calls Little Valley "home to 24 well-maintained courts" and says that "The growth of the programs aids in maintaining the courts, which fortifies the cleanliness of the facility for the public". That is a statement about upkeep from six years ago, not a statement about what the courts are made of, and this site does not turn it into one. What the City does make clear is what kind of place each venue is. Little Valley is headed "Little Valley Pickleball Complex" and carries a schedule that numbers its courts from 1 to 33, reserves them in blocks, and books all thirty-three for tournaments. A place whose courts have numbers on a timetable is a pickleball facility rather than a park with lines painted on something else, and it is published here under the venue type dedicated pickleball facility, the first venue on this site to be. Vernon Worthen and Bloomington are published as parks, because the City lists them among its parks and says nothing about how their six and seven courts are laid out or whether any share a slab with tennis. Nothing is stated about whether any court in the city is indoor, outdoor or covered, so the indoor and outdoor breakdowns for St. George stay empty.
slots.local_scene: Forty-six verified courts across three City venues, thirty-three of them at one address. St. George is the first Utah city on this site and the first in Washington County, and it arrives with a venue that ties for the largest single count anywhere here: Little Valley Pickleball Complex's thirty-three matches Albuquerque's Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex and stands ahead of Mesa's twenty-one. Vernon Worthen Park has six courts and Bloomington Park seven. The City's page is unlike most on this site because it is a programme page rather than an inventory. It lists leagues - Winter, Spring, Summer, Endless Summer and Fall - youth and adult academies, clinics, tournaments and a teaching-court schedule, under a Tennis and Pickleball Head Pro, Wayne P. Bullock. Its own 2020 article says that in 2012 Bullock "established the first pickleball program for the City of St. George on four permanent and two temporary courts at Vernon Worthen Park", that he launched the ladder-league format there and that "the USA Pickleball Association contacted Bullock for permission to adopt it", and that the Little Valley complex was chosen as "Public Facility of the Year" by the Professional Pickleball Registry. The same article says Little Valley was then "home to 24 well-maintained courts"; the City's undated current list says thirty-three, and the current list is what publishes, with the 2020 figure printed as what the venue was. The City is protective of its programme: it asks players to "report non-city / unauthorized clinics, lessons, tournaments, or camps to the Parks Department", requires a court reservation and possibly a special event permit for non-City events, and asks that the reservation be displayed on the court. One venue is refused. The City's list reads "Ledges / ? / Courts: 4", a question mark where the address should be, and this site requires an address that resolves. Price is stated once, in the 2020 article, and only for Little Valley: "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge". Vernon Worthen and Bloomington carry no price, no hours, no lighting and no surface.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts in one place
best_for.text: Little Valley Pickleball Complex has thirty-three courts, the largest count in Utah on this site and tied for the largest anywhere here. It is a programmed facility: the City reserves courts for leagues, clinics and tournaments on a published schedule, an attendant tells you what is free, and the City states that vacant courts are free of charge. Hours, lighting and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to play where the programme began
best_for.text: Vernon Worthen Park is where the City's pickleball programme began in 2012, on "four permanent and two temporary courts" in the City's own words, and where the ladder-league format later adopted by USA Pickleball was launched. Six courts today at a Utah grid address, 300 S. 400 E., near the centre of the city. Price, hours, lighting and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want courts with no timetable attached
best_for.text: Bloomington Park has seven courts and none of the apparatus of Little Valley - no published schedule, no reserved blocks, no attendant to check in with. The City states the name, the address and the count and nothing else, so what you get is seven courts in the south-west of the city with the price, hours, lighting and surface unstated. Seven courts is seven games at once.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does St. George have?
faqs.a: Forty-six across three City venues, all stated on one page: thirty-three at Little Valley Pickleball Complex, seven at Bloomington Park and six at Vernon Worthen Park. The City also lists Ledges with four courts and prints "?" where its address should be, so it is not published. Fifty is the City's own total; forty-six is what this site can place on a map.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in St. George?
faqs.a: Stated at one venue only. The City's 2020 article says of Little Valley that "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge", and the courts are reserved for City programmes on a published schedule. Vernon Worthen and Bloomington carry no price either way, so they are recorded as unknown rather than free, and there is no free filter page for St. George.

faqs.q: Which St. George courts have lights?
faqs.a: Not stated at any venue. The City never uses the word on its pickleball page, and this site publishes lighting only when the operator writes it. Little Valley's schedule runs league sessions until 8:30 and 9:30 p.m. in January, which is a fact about the timetable and not a statement about lamps, so lighting there is recorded as not verified.

Because the City publishes no address for it. Its own list reads "Ledges / ? / Courts: 4", a question mark where the other three lines carry a street address, and this site requires a street address that resolves. The question mark is asserted on every build, so if the City supplies the address, the build stops and Ledges is read again.

faqs.q: Why does Little Valley show 33 courts when the City's article says 24?
faqs.a: Because the two figures are different kinds of record. The City's undated current list says "Little Valley / 2149 Horseman Park Drive / Courts:  33". An article on the same page, dated 19 August 2020, says the complex was then "home to 24 well-maintained courts". A dated record that describes itself as history does not contradict a current list, so thirty-three publishes and twenty-four is printed as what the venue was.
